title: quercus gambelii subsp. vreelandii
intro: Quercus gambelii subsp. vreelandii, commonly known as Vreeland's Gambel oak, is a subspecies of the Gambel oak tree, native to the southwestern United States and Mexico. This plant has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include the potential health benefits of reducing inflammation and improving cardiovascular health due to its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Vreeland's Gambel oak are thought to be attributed to its ability to act as an antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and vasodilator, which can help to lower blood pressure and improve circulation. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
